lessons.title: Percentages, discounts and VAT
lessons.html:
Numbers in business

Supervisors in an abattoir or meat plant deal with prices, wages, yields, stock and costs every day. Accurate calculations prevent losses and help you make good decisions.

Working with percentages

Percent means 'out of 100'. To find a percentage of an amount, multiply the amount by the percentage and divide by 100.

Example: 15% of R2 400 = 2 400 × 15 ÷ 100 = R360.

To find what percentage one number is of another, divide and multiply by 100. If 36 out of 600 carcasses had bruising, then 36 ÷ 600 × 100 = 6%.

Discounts

A butchery buys meat worth R18 000 and gets a 5% discount for paying cash.

  • Discount = 18 000 × 5 ÷ 100 = R900
  • Amount payable = 18 000 − 900 = R17 100

VAT

In South Africa, VAT is charged at the standard rate set by SARS, currently 15%. Some basic foods are zero-rated, so always check which rate applies to the product. To add 15% VAT to a price excluding VAT, multiply by 1.15. To find the price excluding VAT from a VAT-inclusive price, divide by 1.15.

ItemCalculationResult
Price excl. VAT R1 0001 000 × 1.15R1 150 incl. VAT
Price incl. VAT R2 3002 300 ÷ 1.15R2 000 excl. VAT
VAT portion of R2 3002 300 − 2 000R300

Percentage increase

If the price of feed rises from R4 000 to R4 400 per ton, the increase is R400. 400 ÷ 4 000 × 100 = 10% increase.

lessons.title: Costs, profit and wages
lessons.html:
Understanding costs and profit

Cost price, selling price and profit

  • Cost price: what it costs to buy or produce an item.
  • Selling price: what the customer pays.
  • Gross profit = selling price − cost price.
  • Mark-up % = profit ÷ cost price × 100.
  • Profit margin % = profit ÷ selling price × 100.

Example: a carton of mince costs R400 to produce and sells for R500. Profit = R100. Mark-up = 100 ÷ 400 × 100 = 25%. Margin = 100 ÷ 500 × 100 = 20%. Notice mark-up and margin are different; always say which one you mean.

Fixed and variable costs

Fixed costs stay the same whatever the volume, such as rent and insurance. Variable costs change with volume, such as packaging, electricity used by the line and casual labour. Knowing these helps calculate the cost per carcass. If fixed costs are R60 000 a month and the plant slaughters 1 200 cattle, fixed cost per animal is R50. If volume rises to 1 500, it drops to R40 each.

Wages and overtime

A worker earns R32 per hour and works 45 normal hours plus 6 hours overtime paid at 1.5 times the normal rate.

  • Normal pay: 45 × R32 = R1 440
  • Overtime rate: R32 × 1.5 = R48
  • Overtime pay: 6 × R48 = R288
  • Gross pay: R1 440 + R288 = R1 728

Gross pay is before deductions such as UIF, tax and other agreed deductions. Net pay is what the worker receives. Check the current overtime rules in the Basic Conditions of Employment Act and any agreement that applies to your workplace.

lessons.title: Ratios, yields and checking your work
lessons.html:
Ratios and yields in a meat plant

Ratios

A ratio compares two quantities. If a cleaning chemical must be mixed 1 part chemical to 50 parts water (1:50), then for 10 litres of chemical you need 500 litres of water. Always use the dilution on the product label.

Staff ratios: if one supervisor is needed for every 15 workers, 60 workers need 60 ÷ 15 = 4 supervisors.

Dressing yield

Dressing percentage (yield) compares carcass weight with live weight.

Yield % = carcass weight ÷ live weight × 100.

A steer weighs 450 kg live and gives a 252 kg cold carcass. Yield = 252 ÷ 450 × 100 = 56%. Supervisors compare yields to spot problems such as excessive trimming or animals that were not properly rested.

Averages

Average carcass weight = total weight ÷ number of carcasses. If 20 carcasses weigh 4 600 kg in total, the average is 230 kg.

Simple interest

If the business borrows R50 000 at 12% simple interest per year for 2 years: interest = 50 000 × 12 ÷ 100 × 2 = R12 000.

Checking calculations

  • Estimate first: 15% of R2 400 should be a bit more than 10% (R240).
  • Use the reverse operation: if 2 300 ÷ 1.15 = 2 000, check that 2 000 × 1.15 = 2 300.
  • Check units: kilograms, rand and hours must not be mixed up.
  • Use a calculator carefully and enter numbers twice for important figures.
  • Round money to two decimal places (cents).

Key points

  • To find a percentage, multiply by the percentage and divide by 100.
  • Multiply by 1.15 to add 15% VAT; divide by 1.15 to remove it.
  • Mark-up is profit over cost; margin is profit over selling price.
  • Yield % = carcass weight ÷ live weight × 100.
  • Always estimate and check your calculations.
